We're working through Redwood's security questionnaire for our vendor intake and have a few outstanding asks from Legal and Privacy before we can complete approval. Can you please provide the following by 2026-09-07: 

1) An annotated dataflow diagram showing where MedicaSys PII (identifiers, health attributes) is collected, processed, cached, and stored, including all transient caches (KV cache) and any telemetry paths.

We're attaching our intake form (MedicaSys_SSQ_v3.pdf) for your reference. If any of this needs a follow-up call, our legal lead (copied) is available next week.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Dylan / team — draft package attached and notes below. Attachments: redwood-dataflow-medicasys-annotated.png (annotated), subprocessor-roster-medicasys.csv (roster).

Key points (summary):
- Dataflow: MedicaSys PII reaches Redwood via API (ingest), hits inference runtime (ephemeral KV cache per request), and if customer enables telemetry/analytics, a subset of telemetry (non-PII by default) is stored in telemetry DB. Customer-controlled models and inputs can be configured to avoid telemetry capture. See annotated diagram for exact flows.
- Retention: Default operational logs: 30 days. KV cache is ephemeral and scoped to request lifetime (max 1 hour unless pinned by customer). Persistent artefacts (customer-train/artifacts/backups) retained per contract; default retention for customer-provided persistent data is 90 days unless otherwise negotiated in DPA annex.
- Expedited deletion: Customers submit deletion via Console or API; standard SLA for deletion of customer data (non-replicated, non-backup) is 7 business days. Restoration/rollback requests have additional controls. We also provide a deletion certificate on request.
- Access controls: Role-based access, SCIM integration optional, SSO + 2FA enforced for staff. Privileged access requires ticket + approval; separated duties between infra and product teams.

Inline items needing confirmation from Neha: SCC/transfer mechanisms and any in-region hosting offering.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Security Analyst

Adding SCC/transfer and KMS notes for the package — attaching kms-attestation-2026-07.pdf and a DocuSign link for the DPA.

- Cross-border transfers: For customers in the EU we offer SCCs (controller-processor and processor-processor variants) and maintain a transfer assessment. If a customer requires data to remain in-region, Redwood has a Dedicated/Private deployment option to host in EU-only regions (TOS/ops annex applies).
- KMS: Default hosted offering uses Redwood-managed KMS; keys reside in provider KMS per region. We support customer-managed keys (CMK) via standard KMS integrations (customer-owned AWS/GCP keys) for Dedicated/Private deployments; HSM-backed options available on request. Attached attestation describes our key custody model and separation of key usage for telemetry vs. customer payloads.
- Subprocessor contracts: All subprocessors have DPAs or DPA addenda; the CSV includes DPA status column.

DocuSign link (DPA envelope): https://docusign.example.com/MS-DPA-042

- Retention & deletion: Default retention windows above; expedited deletion SLA 7 business days for active copies. Backups require mutual agreement for deletion timelines — we provide deletion certificates where requested.
- Subprocessors: CSV contains all subprocessors that touch customer payloads or telemetry. For Dedicated customers we can offer a reduced roster.
- Transfer mechanisms: For EU customers we offer SCCs as standard; Dedicated/private deployments available for in-region-only hosting.
- KMS: Default Redwood-managed KMS; CMK/HSM available for Dedicated/Private. See attestation.

Next steps: please confirm if you want (1) an in-person review with our Security/Privacy team, (2) DPA countersign via the DocuSign link, or (3) an annex for in-region hosting. If Legal wants any of the retention numbers tightened, we can propose contractual annex language.
